properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 28 at 4:57PM MDT until September 28 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Kane County in southern Utah...
East Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 457 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across portions of Zion National Park, and additional
heavier rain is anticipated to move into the area over the next
hour. Up to 0.25 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons, normally
dry washes, creeks and streams.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zion National Park and Springdale.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 28 at 3:56PM PDT until September 28 at 4:45PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
SVRVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
West Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...

* Until 445 PM MST.

* At 356 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles south of
Meadview, or 42 miles east of Boulder City, moving northeast at 25
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Meadview, Grand Canyon Ranch, South Cove and Pierce Ferry And
Antares Roads.
properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 28 at 5:49PM CDT until September 29 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS Grand Forks ND
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of west central Minnesota, including the following
county, Clay and southeast North Dakota, including the following
counties, Barnes, Cass and Ransom.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Recent rainfall has saturated soils in portions of southeast
North Dakota into southern Red River Valley of Minnesota.
Potential for additional 3 to 5 inches of rainfall presents
potential for flash flooding to occur late this afternoon through
tonight.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Eastern
Juab/Millard Counties, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch
Plateau/Book Cliffs, Western Millard and Juab Counties and
Southwest Utah.

* WHEN...From 6 AM MDT this morning through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

- Deep tropical moisture will combine with an upper level low
crossing the Desert Southwest to bring an increased threat of
flash flooding through late tonight. Widespread rainfall totals
of 0.75 to 1.75 inches, with locally higher amounts in excess of
2 inches will occur.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 27 at 8:56PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Strong southwesterly winds ahead of a closed low centered over
California will pull tropical moisture from Tropical Storm Odalys and
Hurricane Polo towards eastern Utah and western Colorado, with
atmospheric moisture peaking in our area on Monday. The northerly
extent of the expected excessive rainfall poses a threat to our
southern San Juan river basins. Current forecasts suggest 1 to 4
inches of rain Monday morning through early Wednesday. At face value,
rivers and tributaries will see a rise due to the forecast rainfall.
However, localized heavier amounts could result in flooding across
the southern San Juan foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been recently observed.
However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts (i.e. above 90th
percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action stage to minor
flooding. Most probable basins to see significant rises include; the
Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito Creek, and the
Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA. However, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Confidence has increased enough for a Flood Watch to be issued
for southern portions of the forecast area valid from 6AM Monday
through 6AM Wednesday. Continue to monitor the latest forecasts
especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in the Watch
areas.

AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Monday, September 28, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Monday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

properties.description:
Cooler temperatures will allow for the first chance for snowfall
accumulations. While snow could be seen in some low lying areas in
and around Fairbanks, the best chance for accumulations will be
at higher elevations. Snowfall accumulations from Monday night
through Wednesday night are expected to be between 1" and 3". Any
snow that falls in the lower elevations will be very wet and will
mostly likely melt during the day with high temperatures remaining
in the low 40s.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
